MetricsQueryMetadata.description: Object containing all metric names returned and their associated metadata.

end.description: End of the time window, milliseconds since Unix epoch.

interval.description: Number of milliseconds between data samples.

pointlist.description: List of points of the timeseries in milliseconds.

query_index.description: The index of the series' query within the request.

scope.description: Metric scope, comma separated list of tags.

start.description: Start of the time window, milliseconds since Unix epoch.

unit.description:
Detailed information about the metric unit.
The first element describes the "primary unit" (for example, `bytes` in `bytes per second`).
The second element describes the "per unit" (for example, `second` in `bytes per second`).
If the second element is not present, the API returns null.

MetricsQueryResponse.description: Response Object that includes your query and the list of metrics retrieved.

error.description: Message indicating the errors if status is not `ok`.

from_date.description: Start of requested time window, milliseconds since Unix epoch.

group_by.description: List of tag keys on which to group.

items.description: Tag key to group by your metric.

to_date.description: End of requested time window, milliseconds since Unix epoch.

MetricsQueryUnit.description: Object containing the metric unit family, scale factor, name, and short name.

family.description: Unit family, allows for conversion between units of the same family, for scaling.

plural.description: Plural form of the unit name.

scale_factor.description: Factor for scaling between units of the same family.

items.description:
Each point is of the form `[POSIX_timestamp, numeric_value]`.
The timestamp should be in seconds and current.
The numeric value format should be a 32bit float gauge-type value.
Current is defined as not more than 10 minutes in the future or more than 1 hour in the past.
